chunks.title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - Custom Texture Highlight Lines
chunks.content: ## Custom Texture Highlight Lines in CLO This section explains the process of creating and applying custom texture highlight lines—referred to as "famous lines"—in CLO software. It covers terminology such as SPI (Stitches Per Inch), image sizing, and how these affect the texture and appearance of highlight lines. ### Understanding SPI and Image Preparation - **SPI (Stitches Per Inch)** defines the number of frames or stitches within one inch. - The length of the famous line texture is determined by the SPI value. - To prepare the texture image: - Change the unit size of the image to inches. - Set the width of the image corresponding to the desired number of inches based on SPI. - Pay attention to the height of the image for correct scaling. - Save the texture as a PNG file before importing into CLO. ### Creating and Applying the Famous Line Texture - In CLO, create a new famous line and switch to the custom texture option. - Import the prepared PNG image as the well-treated famous line texture. - Example: If the texture width is 0.5 inches, with SPI set to 2, this means two frames per inch. - Select the "SPIR" setting and switch the line unit to millimeters for precision (e.g., 8.89 mm). - This millimeter value affects the scaling and application of the texture on the famous line. - Input the desired values based on the texture and garment specifications. ### Adjusting the Famous Line on the Garment - Use the free famous line tool to add the texture highlight line to the garment board. - Enlarge the 3D window details for precise inspection. - To make the famous line appear cut with the garment: - Set the well-treated texture height value to half the height of the famous line. - Check the overall visual effect to ensure proper integration of the highlight line. ### Generating and Correcting the Well-Treated Image - Use the auto-generated PBR (Physically Based Rendering) sticker feature to generate the well-treated texture image. - Click "Generate" and then browse to locate the image. - Note: The generated well-treated image may appear upside down. - To correct this: - Turn off the automatic orientation. - Change the well-treated strength value to negative to invert the image properly. - Inspect the famous line closely: - Small cracks may appear between texture segments; this requires careful adjustment. - Once corrected, the famous line is effectively cut and integrated with the garment surface, enhancing realism. --- This guide provides detailed steps and technical considerations for preparing and applying custom texture highlight lines ("famous lines") in CLO, emphasizing image sizing, SPI settings, and texture orientation for optimal 3D garment visualization.
